decls.description: The generic capabilities, the one vocabulary of the core. A pack says what a capability reads through its own read rules; holding one grants nothing by itself.

agent.description: an automated reader or proposer, not a person

read.description: reads what the pack's read rules give this capability

read_restricted.description: reads the restricted sources the pack's read rules give this capability

decls.description: A role at the gate, as the deploy profile names it (access.roles).

slots.description: The capabilities the pack maps this role to: pack data, never code. A read rule of the form may_read(r, "K", x) :- role__capability(r, "c"), K(x). gives kind K in full to every role with a row (r, c) here, and that row is the evidence the checker recomputes (docs/architecture.md, access and privacy).

lines: // The shared typed read right (S28, O8). Each consumer supplies its own grant clauses.
// This declaration alone denotes the empty set and confers no read rights.
.decl may_read(role: symbol, kind: symbol, element: symbol)
// Explicit full-kind read coverage (decisions/central-read-access.md). Each consumer supplies
// its own coverage clauses; this declaration alone denotes the empty set and grants no coverage.

module.description: Roles in two layers. A role is an element like any other: the pack names its roles as facts, and its rules derive which typed elements a role may read, as may_read(role, kind, element). Rezono knows only the generic capabilities below; a pack maps each of its roles to capabilities as facts (role__capability), and its read rules may grant a kind to every role that holds a capability.
